team: Andrea Cutroni, Elena Corio, Symon Kipkemei, Giovanni Carlo Volpe
description: Spatial-network analysis of three European cohousing projects, testing whether circulation design can be engineered for chance social encounters.
body: Traditional housing corridors are often socially inert. This study applies spatial-network, space-syntax and visibility analyses — closeness, betweenness and degree centrality, isovists and shortest paths — to three built cohousing projects: Wohnprojekt Wien, Gleis21 and Spreefeld Berlin.

Comparing double-loaded, perimeter and point-block circulation typologies shows that high connectivity and visual openness systematically drive chance encounters between residents — evidence that circulation design can shift community-building from an intuitive judgment call to a data-driven design decision.
